judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the over-generalization of the SN 1987A cooling bound on g_{ap} from Lella:2023bfb, nor challenge the missing mass/coupling conditions. The only citation-related flag concerns impossible publication years.

The review mentions only impossible/future publication years and missing journal information in the bibliography. It does not challenge the SN 1987A cooling-bound claim tied to Lella:2023bfb or note that its mass/coupling conditions are overgeneralised.

The reviewer flags a publication year error for Reference 13 (Lella 2023), but does not challenge the claim sentence itself or mention the over-generalization of the axion mass and coupling scope as required by detection rule A.
The reviewer does not mention the inconsistency between 10^{-8} eV and 10^{-9} eV in the Light axions subsection. No numerical inconsistency related to the mass threshold is flagged.

The reviewer does not mention the inconsistent Milky-Way-dominated mass threshold in the 'Light axions' subsection, nor any discrepancy between 10^-8 eV and 10^-9 eV. No numerical inconsistency of this kind is flagged.

The reviewer mentions 'factual typos' and a publication year error for Ref 6, but fails to identify or challenge the specific inconsistent mass threshold value (10^-8 eV) as required by detection rule B.

The reviewer does not flag the local notation change from g_{a\gamma} to g_{\gamma a} in the SMM Galactic-conversion bound sentence. The notation unification comment in Major Issue 1 refers to \omega_a vs E_a, not g_{a\gamma} vs g_{\gamma a}.

Although the reviewer notes that an equation uses both ω_a and E_a and asks to unify notation, they do not identify the specific local symbol drift from g_{aγ} to g_{γa} in Sec. 3.1. The flagged notation issue concerns energy symbols, not the axion-photon coupling notation.

The reviewer mentions 'notational inconsistencies' in the summary and specifically cites an inconsistency between omega_a and E_a in Equation 3, but does not flag the injected notation drift from g_{a gamma} to g_{gamma a} in Section 3.1.
